name: Public Library Teen Volunteers
description: Help shelve books, set up summer reading events, read to younger kids, or help with craft and tech programs. Libraries are calm, supervised public places.
howToStart: Ask at the front desk of your local public library about teen volunteer programs.

name: Local Food Bank or Food Pantry
description: Sort donated food, pack boxes for families, and help at food drives. Great to do with friends or family, and you can see the difference right away.
howToStart: With a trusted adult, look up the food bank or pantry that serves your town and sign up for a group shift.

name: Animal Shelter or Humane Society
description: Make toys and blankets for shelter pets, help with cleaning and laundry, socialize cats, or help at adoption events. Younger volunteers usually work alongside a parent.
howToStart: Ask a trusted adult to check your local shelter’s website for youth or family volunteer programs.

name: Park, Beach, or Trail Clean-Up
description: Pick up litter, plant trees and flowers, or help care for trails at events run by your town’s parks department or a nature group.
howToStart: Look for clean-up days on your town’s parks and recreation page with a trusted adult.

name: Senior Center or Retirement Community
description: Play games, help with crafts, perform music, or teach older adults how to use their phones. Many seniors love talking with young people.
howToStart: With a trusted adult, call your town’s senior center and ask about youth volunteers.

name: Boys & Girls Club or Community Youth Center
description: Help younger kids with homework, games, sports, and art activities. Staff are always there to supervise.
howToStart: Ask the staff at your local club or youth center about junior volunteer or junior staff programs.

name: Community Garden
description: Plant, water, and harvest vegetables. Some gardens give food to local pantries, so you help feed people too.
howToStart: With a trusted adult, ask your town or a local garden club about volunteer days.

name: Habitat for Humanity ReStore
description: Help sort, price, and organize donated furniture and building supplies. The money raised helps build homes for families.
howToStart: Ask a trusted adult to check your nearest ReStore’s youth volunteer rules.

name: Charity Walk or Fun Run Helper
description: Hand out water, cheer runners, help with sign-in, or set up and clean up at a charity race. Lots of energy and fun with friends.
howToStart: With a trusted adult, look for charity walks or runs in your town and sign up as a volunteer.

name: School Service Club or Tutoring
description: Join your school’s service club, tutor younger students, or help teachers with events. It’s right at school, so it’s easy to get to.
howToStart: Ask your school counselor which service clubs or tutoring programs count for volunteer hours.

name: Hospital Junior Volunteers
description: Deliver flowers and mail, help at the gift shop, or make cards for patients. A great fit if you’re thinking about a health career.
howToStart: Ask a trusted adult to look up your local hospital’s junior or teen volunteer program and its age rules.

name: Community Arts or Music Events
description: Help set up festivals, paint murals, run kids’ craft tables, or play music at community events.
howToStart: With a trusted adult, check your town’s arts council or community calendar for volunteer spots.
